image_description: A group of smiling graduates wearing black academic gowns and mortarboard caps. The central figure is a female graduate holding a diploma, flanked by a male graduate in a blue gown on the left and others in the background. The image captures a celebratory graduation moment with shallow depth of field blurring the background.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Flowing full-length garment with rectangular silhouette draping from shoulders to ankles.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The subjects are shown in a medium close-up shot (waist/chest up). The lower portion of the gowns extending to the ankles is completely outside the frame, making it impossible to verify the full-length rectangular silhouette.

The visible upper torso of the gowns shows a clear vertical division down the center front, consistent with the open-front design of academic regalia. The drape appears symmetrical relative to the wearer's body.
The fabric hangs loosely around the shoulders and chest, effectively hiding the specific shape of the arms and torso underneath, matching the 'voluminous' description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Wide open sleeves extending well below hand level.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: While the sleeve openings are visible near the shoulders/arms, the actual length and termination point of the sleeves (whether they extend past the hands) are obscured by the subjects' poses (holding diplomas/caps) and the cropping of the image.
The distinct vertical edges of the front panels are visible on the central subject, creating the characteristic open look of the gown.
Collars of shirts or other garments are visible at the neckline beneath the gowns, indicating they are worn over other clothes.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Heavy matte fabric typically black polyester or wool blend.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The fabric absorbs light rather than reflecting it sharply, appearing matte and relatively heavy/thick, consistent with traditional gown materials.
No specular highlights or glossy textures are observed on the black fabric; the surface appears uniform and smooth.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Characteristic sleeve drape extending past the wrist.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Similar to the functional component checkpoint, the full extent of the sleeve drape is not visible due to framing and pose occlusion.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The faces in the background exhibit slight 'waxy' smoothing and lack fine skin texture detail, typical of AI generation or aggressive denoising. The mortarboard caps in the background have slightly soft, ill-defined edges compared to the foreground.

The hand holding the rolled diploma appears anatomically ambiguous. The fingers seem to merge into the paper roll without clear separation, and the grip structure looks physically implausible (fingers appear to pass through or melt into the object).
The tassel on the central subject's cap hangs with a slight unnatural stiffness and the attachment point to the button is somewhat indistinct, blending into the cap fabric.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific type of garment matches the 'academic gown' class label and distinguish it from similar robes (e.g., judicial or religious).
To audit the structural integrity of the hands and arms, specifically checking for fused fingers or extra limbs which are common AI artifacts in complex poses like holding objects.
To check for edge bleeding between the black gowns and the background/skin, and to ensure the mortarboard caps are topologically sound (flat planes, correct corners).
To assess the overall coherence of lighting and texture consistency across the multiple subjects, identifying any subtle generative inconsistencies.

focus_areas: Gown fabric texture and drape realism
Mortarboard cap geometry and tassel physics
Facial feature consistency in background subjects
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the central subject's hand holding the diploma. AI models often struggle with finger articulation around cylindrical objects. Verify if the fingers are distinct or if they merge/melt into the paper. Also, inspect the transition between the black gown and the skin/neckline for any haloing or color bleeding artifacts.
